purpose: Construct an exact topology-preserving remesh as a cochain retract and identify its reconstruction projector and unresolved fine modes.

chainMaps.meaning: S subdivides the coarse face into three fine faces; F collapses the centre vertex to coarse vertex 0.

cochainMaps.meaning: Both maps commute with d and R_k T_k=I on every coarse degree.

reconstruction.definition: P_k=T_k R_k on fine cochains; Q_k=I-P_k
reconstruction.meaning: P is an idempotent chain projector onto coarse-representable fine data; Q records internal fine modes erased by restriction.

metricBoundary.conclusion: Chain-safe transport is not automatically an isometry. The Euclidean least-squares reconstruction is an orthogonal projector but fails the cochain commuting gate, so energy optimality and gauge safety cannot be merged by assumption.

rdgInterpretation.gamma: restriction R extracts the coarse relational state
rdgInterpretation.sigma: reconstruction T, or P=TR when acting on fine data
rdgInterpretation.delta: Q=I-TR is the unresolved fine-scale residual
rdgInterpretation.qGate: admit a remesh only when T and R commute with d and declared metric/energy tolerances also pass

verdict: A nontrivial topology-preserving geometry change can be made gauge-safe through a cochain retract. It yields an exact RDG-style reconstruction projector and residual detector, but metric and energy compatibility remain independent gates.
